title: 11 For what cauſe God would not haue vs certaine of the time of iudgement.

segments.text: ALbeit it be moſt certaine, that the laſt iudgement ſhal at length be: yet the day of that iudgement is altogether vncertaine. Mar. 13.32. Of that day, and houre, no man knoweth, no not the Angels which are in heauen; nor the Sonne himſelfe; ſaue the Father. Wherefore the yeare, moneth, day, houre of the laſt iudgement, Chriſt himſelfe alſo knoweth not, not onely as concerning his humane nature, but alſo in reſpect of his preſent office. The preſent office of Chriſt, to wit, in that he is our Mediatour, doth not require, that he ſhould declare that vnto vs. Now the cauſes why God would haue it hid from vs, are theſe. 1 That he might exerciſe our faith and patience, and ſo we ſhould ſhew that we would beleeue God, albeit wee knowe not the time of our deliuerie. 2 That he might bridle our curioſitie. 3 That he might keepe vs in his feare, in godlineſſe, and in executing of our dutie: and ſo we ſhould bee readie euery moment. Mat. 24.43. Jf the good-man of the houſe knew. Luk. 12.40. Occupie til I come.
